bottleneck: Commercial DNA synthesis can be misused to assemble pathogens, yet screening of orders is voluntary, inconsistent across providers, and blind to novel or heavily engineered sequences that evade pathogen lists. As synthesis gets cheaper and more distributed — including benchtop synthesizers — centralized screening becomes unenforceable. AI-designed proteins with no natural counterpart defeat list-based screening entirely, and the gap between synthesis capability and oversight widens yearly.
current_state: The International Gene Synthesis Consortium screens members' orders against pathogen lists, but non-member and in-house synthesis escape oversight. Sequence-based screening for novel threats does not exist at scale.
title: DNA synthesis screening cannot catch novel threats
why_it_blocks: Democratized DNA writing without commensurate oversight is a biosecurity time bomb. The bottleneck is not technology but governance that scales with the technology — and governance is losing the race.
